insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (varies as per Policy Schedule)

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: We will reset up to 100% of the Annual Sum Insured, for any illness/disease/injury for the Insured Person in a Policy Year... i. This benefit will be triggered unlimited times for any illness/disease/injury.
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 11. Reset Benefit
great.explanation: Up to 100% of the Annual Sum Insured is restored for any illness/disease/injury, and it can trigger unlimited times in a policy year. This can significantly increase available cover if the sum insured gets exhausted due to multiple hospitalisations.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
great.quote: We will cover the Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses... immediately 90 days before the Insured Person’s Admission to Hospital
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 4. Pre-Hospitalisation Medical Expenses
great.explanation: Pre-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for 90 days immediately before hospital admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests and medicines leading up to hospitalisation.

great.name: NCB
great.quote: We will provide a Loyalty Bonus of 20%... at the end of each Policy Year irrespective of a claim being initiated... ix. In the event of Claim, under the Policy during any subsequent Policy Year, the credited Loyalty Bonus will not be reduced.
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 10. Loyalty Bonus
great.explanation: A 20% Loyalty Bonus is added at the end of each policy year even if a claim is made, and it is not reduced after future claims. This is stronger than typical no-claim bonuses that drop or reset after a claim.

great.name: Bariatric Surgery
great.quote: We will cover medical expenses incurred in respect of Hospitalisation of the Insured Person for Surgical Procedure/treatment for Obesity up to Annual Sum Insured
great.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 12. Bariatric Surgery Cover
great.explanation: Hospitalisation expenses for surgical procedure/treatment for obesity are covered up to the Annual Sum Insured. This is a valuable inclusion because many retail health plans exclude bariatric surgery or cover it only via add-ons.

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: Room Rent charges up to Single Private AC room;
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 1. In-patient Treatment
good.explanation: Room rent is covered up to a Single Private AC room. Staying in a higher category room can lead to reduced claim payout due to linked room-rent conditions.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED)... shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > 1. Pre-Existing Diseases - Code- Excl01
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for the first 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. Claims for declared/known conditions during this period can be rejected.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > 2. Specified Disease/Procedure Waiting Period - Code- Excl02
good.explanation: Listed specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months of continuous coverage. This is a common market waiting period for certain planned surgeries and conditions.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Exclusions > Standard Exclusions > 4. 30-day waiting period - Code- Excl03
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered in the first 30 days from the first policy commencement date, except for accidents. Early claims for sickness during this period can be denied.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: We will cover the Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses... immediately 180 days following the Insured Person’s discharge from Hospital
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 5. Post Hospitalization Medical Expenses
good.explanation: Post-hospitalisation medical expenses are covered for 180 days immediately after discharge. This helps cover follow-up consultations, diagnostics and medicines for a longer recovery period.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: We will cover the expenses incurred on Air Ambulance services up to the Annual Sum Insured...
good.reference: Add ons/Optional Covers > 12. Domestic Air Ambulance Cover
good.explanation: Air ambulance expenses are covered up to the Annual Sum Insured under an optional add-on. This can be useful for emergency transfers but will apply only if you buy the add-on.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: We will cover the Medical Expenses incurred in respect of the Domiciliary Hospitalization of the Insured Person during the Policy Period up to the Annual Sum Insured
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 9. Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.explanation: Domiciliary hospitalisation (treatment at home when hospitalisation is required) is covered up to the Annual Sum Insured, subject to policy conditions. This helps when a hospital bed is unavailable or the patient cannot be moved.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: We will cover... Technological Advancements and Treatments... for the below mentioned... [listed items: Robotic surgeries, Deep Brain stimulation, etc.]
good.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 3. Technological Advancements and Treatments
good.explanation: Coverage is provided for technological advancements and treatments only for the items specifically listed (e.g., robotic surgeries, deep brain stimulation). If a modern treatment is not on the list, it may not be payable even if medically necessary.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: medicines, drugs and consumables (other than those specified in the list of excluded expenses (non-medical) in Annexure II.
bad.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 1. In-patient Treatment (point v) + Annexure II
bad.explanation: Consumables are payable only except those mentioned in the excluded (non-medical) list in Annexure II. This can create out-of-pocket costs for common hospital items that are often billed separately.

bad.name: Proportionate Deduction
bad.quote: If the Insured Person is admitted in a room category/limit that is higher than the one that is specified... then the Insured Person shall bear a proportional share of the total Associated medical expenses
bad.reference: Benefits covered under the Policy > Basic cover > 1. In-patient Treatment (claim conditions)
bad.explanation: If you choose a room category higher than the eligible limit, you must bear a proportional share of the total associated medical expenses. This can sharply reduce the claim payout beyond just the room rent difference.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “Co-Payment” shall mean a cost sharing requirement... A co-payment does not reduce the Sum Insured
bad.reference: Definitions > Co-Payment (definition only); Optional Covers > 19. Voluntary Co-Payment; Optional Cover 29 Network Advantage (20% co-pay outside PPN if opted)
bad.explanation: A co-pay applies if you opt for the Voluntary Co-Payment option or if you opt for the Network Advantage option where a 20% co-pay applies outside the PPN. Any co-pay means you pay part of every claim from your pocket, so opting into these variants reduces claim reimbursement.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
